terms.meaning: The whole of knowledge, arts, morals, law, customs and abilities we learn as members of society. The word comes from Latin "colere", to cultivate.
Many cultures in one society, from different religions and life styles.
Behaviour society expects, such as honesty, cleanliness and patriotism. They help us judge good and bad.
Things we do again and again in daily life without much thought.

items.name: What shapes a culture
items.formula: Geography, traditions and the needs of a society.
items.example: So we can't call one culture good and another bad.

items.name: How culture passes on
items.formula: From one generation to the next.
items.example: The language we speak came from our elders.

items.name: Culture keeps changing
items.formula: Dress, hair styles and food habits change over the years.
items.example: So every society's culture differs too.

items.name: Cultures influence one another
items.formula: The chudidar came to us from elsewhere; trousers, shirts and English from the British.
items.example: Differences don't stop cultures from borrowing.

items.name: Unity in diversity
items.formula: India has hundreds of tribes, thousands of castes, many races and hundreds of languages.
items.example: Walk down a street in Bengaluru and you see this mix.

items.name: Customs and traditions
items.formula: Beliefs, values, rules, conventions and morals, taken together.
items.example: All of these make up a culture.

items.name: Examples of conventions
items.formula: How we eat, sleep and greet people.
items.example: Nobody asks the teacher each day how to sit in class.

mistakes.text: In sociology, culture doesn't mean only good manners. It covers all we learn in society.
Don't rank cultures as better or worse: each is shaped by its own place and needs.
Values are about good and bad. Conventions are daily habits.
